text:
Congratulations to the West Baltimore communities and leaders receiving $4.1 million in community grants tied to the Amtrak Frederick Douglass Tunnel Program. The Tunnel represents a historic federal investment in Baltimore, replacing the 153-year-old B&P Tunnel, rebuilding the West Baltimore MARC station, improving surrounding infrastructure and supporting thousands of jobs. Over ten years, the program will distribute $50 million in grants.

I worked with my colleagues in Congress to help secure this investment and press for protections, mitigation measures and community safeguards for the people who live along the project corridor. As construction moves forward, that Congressional oversight will continue so Baltimore receives the full protections and benefits of this federal investment.

I send my deepest appreciation to Principal Kimberly Hill at Mary Ann Winterling Elementary School for hosting the announcement. Kudos to Luigi Rosa, who leads the project for Amtrak, and to State Senator Antonio Hayes, Councilmen John Bullock and Jermaine Jones, and Comptroller Bill Henry for your work to ensure our constituents take advantage of this federal opportunity.

#FrederickDouglassTunnel #WestBaltimore #Baltimore #FederalInvestment #CommunityInvestment #Infrastructure #Amtrak #Maryland

Every day, our firefighters and first responders put everything on the line to keep our communities safe. In many of our communities, our firefighters are the first on the scene when someone needs help. They battle wildfires, save lives during floods, and provide life-saving care.

That’s why I’ve invested millions in fire and emergency services across our state, including in Albuquerque, Moriarty and the East Mountains, Fort Sumner, Sandia, and Peralta. We have new proposals for emergency centers in Lincoln and Valencia counties. I secured millions with Albuquerque legislators for new fire engines and equipment, and helped pass the state law to ensure our firefighters and first responders can get care for PTSD. (It was, in fact, my first bill signed into law with Rep. Armstrong.)

Since day one, the safety of our communities has been at the forefront of our work, and I am so humbled and grateful to stand with our firefighters every day as they are on the front lines keeping us safe!

text: RT @DarializaforNY: Yesterday, an ICE agent opened fire in Marble Hill. They shot a member of our community in the neck while he was in his…

reposted.text:
Yesterday, an ICE agent opened fire in Marble Hill. They shot a member of our community in the neck while he was in his car. His five-year-old kid was in a child seat in the back of the car when ICE agents fired at least 7 rounds into it. This was in the middle of the afternoon, with children walking home from school and people heading home from work. Federal agents put every one of them in danger.

When I was in Marble Hill last night I saw NYPD officers rapidly escalating violence. As I was trying to de-escalate, I was shoved to the ground by an officer. I witnessed unmarked law enforcement cars hitting protestors as NYPD officers pushed people out of its path. And instead of condemning ICE’s violence, Police Commissioner Tisch attempted to justify the shooting by reading off our neighbor’s past interactions with police.

The NYPD spent more time protecting a militia that just shot someone than protecting New Yorkers. Last night, the NYPD and Commissioner Tisch violated the spirit, if not the letter, of our sanctuary city policies and fueled the Trump Administration’s attempt to demonize our communities. The NYPD’s Strategic Response Group must be disbanded as quickly as possible, and Commissioner Tisch must step down.

In this district, there are mothers who are afraid to send their kids to school, workers who are afraid to show up for their shifts, and people who won’t call for help anymore because they can’t be sure who will come. That’s what it means to have a violent militia operating in your community. You don’t feel safe walking down your own street. 

For decades, we’ve been told ICE can be fixed with more oversight, better training, or reform. But you can’t reform an agency whose purpose is to terrorize immigrant families. You can’t train cruelty out of a system built to enact cruelty. ICE must be abolished.

This moment demands that everyone step up. Elected officials at every level need to stop hedging and say it plainly: Abolish ICE now. Our city must enforce every sanctuary protection we have and city officials must ensure this cannot happen again.

The future of 6G and satellite technology will be decided at next year's World Radiocommunication Conference in China.

The U.S. can't afford to show up without a lead negotiator. I'm urging Secretary Rubio to name one now.

We should be setting the rules, not China. https://t.co/SQfa1eB2BM

quoted.text:
Exclusive: Sens. Ruben Gallego (D-Arizona) and Jim Banks (R-Indiana) sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sept. 29 urging the State Department to “designate a U.S. head of delegation” for the World Radiocommunication Conference 2027, known as WRC-27, in Shanghai. Washington Post Intelligence obtained the letter.

“China is hosting the very conference where the rules for 6G get written, and will use that home-field advantage to push standards favoring Huawei,” Gallego told me. “The U.S. needs a lead negotiator in that room now, not after the rules are locked in.”

The senators argue that hosting could give China more opportunities to shape the agenda, build support for its preferred positions, and influence negotiations around spectrum and technology standards. They also contend that Beijing could use that leverage to advance the interests of Chinese companies such as Huawei. “A strong U.S. delegation, coordinating its position well in advance alongside like-minded allies and partners, is the best defense against the CCP’s authoritarian agenda,” they wrote.

The senators credited the administration with progress on “the substance of U.S. preparations.” Some U.S. proposals have already gone to the Inter‑American Telecommunication Commission (CITEL), the Organization of American States’ telecommunications commission, the letter stated. The rest are due at its meeting in Bogotá beginning Nov. 30. They asked the administration to name a head of delegation before that meeting. They are also asking Rubio to give the Senate more details on the administration’s strategy and positions going into WRC-27.

“Countries around the world are choosing between trusted technology and Chinese surveillance, and Huawei is making door-to-door sales pitches,” Gallego told me. “If the United States doesn’t work with its allies to shape 6G standards now, China will close the deal and bring more countries under their influence. That will pose national security implications for at least a decade, maybe longer.”

text:
As a child experiencing abuse, when I read Maya Angelou’s “I Know Why The Caged Bird Sings,” I knew for the first time that I was not alone in the world. So when we say “books save lives,” we mean it.

That’s why I was so proud to introduce the Books Save Lives Act of 2026 — my bill to confront the rise of book bans in America, promote inclusive literature, and protect our freedom to read.

This fight is about honoring the brilliance of Black and queer authors, educators, students, and librarians—and it’s a fight for education, democracy, and justice.

Because from bans on our bodies to bans on our books, Trump and Republicans are stopping at nothing to rip away our fundamental freedoms, censor Black, queer and other marginalized authors, and deny us the right to learn and see ourselves reflected in our literature.

Thank you to my colleagues and movement partners for your partnership on this legislation.

Congress must pass our bill without delay.

text: Who knew that Oren Cass wasn’t an actual economist. He sure does a job of presenting himself as one. Is often quoted in articles and reputable policy journals. https://t.co/s8FmMfmHCz

quoted.text:
Joe Biden surrounded himself with people who embraced modern monetary theory, a heterodox academic fad that taught you could write as many blank checks as you liked without the consequence of inflation. Larry Summers, Bill Clinton’s Treasury secretary, warned Democrats not to go down that road. Conservative economists warned Democrats not to go down that road. Biden listened instead to the modern monetary theorists and their loud defenders online, ultimately signing a $1.9 trillion spending bill on top of everything else, and gave the country inflation that peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022. Democrats paid for it at the ballot box.

Unfortunately, President Trump has made a similar mistake. He has surrounded himself with men who staked out heterodox views on the economy decades ago and now treat his administration as a laboratory. Peter Navarro has spent his career pushing trade theories that nearly the entire economics profession rejects, and he once propped up his own books by quoting an expert named Ron Vara, who turned out to be Peter Navarro.

Outside the White House, Oren Cass, a lawyer and former management consultant with no formal training in economics, founded a think tank, gave himself the title of chief economist, and has become the most prominent defender of the tariffs on the right. Around them is a chorus of loud social media defenders who insist tariffs are a tax on foreigners.

The MMT crowd promised that massive spending would not cause inflation. It did. The tariff crowd promised that tariffs would not raise prices or hurt wages. They did both. We no longer have to argue about it as a matter of theory. We have the data. The tariffs raised prices and held down wages.

The administration now refuses to change course. That is arrogance. It is also bad politics. The tariff regime has turned into a favor generator, with exemptions going to whoever hires the right lobbyist. Voters now rank corruption as a top concern for the first time in a generation. Republicans are heading into a midterm with voters angry about prices, angry about corruption, and trusting Democrats more than Republicans on the economy. Much of that is self-inflicted, and the tariffs are the biggest self-inflicted wound of all.

https://t.co/GHztwD67oC

I was proud to present @Caltech’s Dr. François Tissot, an Eaton Fire survivor, with a Certificate of Congressional Recognition for receiving an @NSF award to advance critical research on toxic contamination following wildfires.

For families devastated by the Eaton Fire, the question of when their homes are safe remains urgently unanswered. Lead and other dangerous contaminants pose serious health risks, yet families still lack clear, science-based guidance on when they can safely return. With this funding, Dr. Tissot and his team will bring scientists, insurers, and affected communities together to help close that gap and improve how we assess and respond to contamination after wildfires nationwide.

Because no family recovering from a wildfire should have to wonder whether the home they're returning to is safe.

“President Trump’s decision to launch an unnecessary war of choice with Iran has been disastrous. The war has resulted in the deaths of at least 19 service members and more than 800 wounded, over $40 billion in taxpayer dollars spent, thousands of civilians killed and injured, spiking gas prices, rising costs for everyday American families, and further regional instability. 

"The administration has not accomplished its strategic objectives after over seven months of war. The President is in denial and continues to insist on prosecuting this war despite a lack of evidence and coherent strategy for how the war can achieve its aims. It is far past time for President Trump to wake up to reality and evaluate the real options on the table that will best serve the interests of the American people and our regional partners. 

"It should be obvious by now that the only logical end to this war is a negotiated settlement achieved through diplomatic engagement by skilled negotiators, similar to the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action President Trump destroyed, before it continues to spiral even more out of control. We need actual diplomats working to achieve actual peace."

On this day in 2012, Malala Yousafzai was targeted and shot by the Taliban for speaking out in support of girls education in Pakistan. 

Rather than silencing her voice, the attack brought greater international attention to the barriers preventing millions of girls from receiving an education. Malala survived and continued advocating for every child’s right to learn, later becoming the youngest-ever recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize.  

Today, we recognize Malala’s courage and the continued fight for equal access to education around the world.

You’re not going to believe this.

Before Todd Blanche was the Attorney General, he was the Deputy Attorney General.

And when he took that job, he held between $159,000 and $485,000 in cryptocurrency and crypto-related investments.

He made two promises: get rid of those investments, and until he did, stay out of anything that could directly affect his financial interests in crypto.

A month into the job, while he STILL OWNED THE CRYPTO, he ordered investigations into crypto companies, dealers, and exchanges to be shut down and disbanded an enforcement team tasked with investigating crypto fraud and money laundering.

Then, more than a month later, he finally “divested,” except he didn’t “sell” most of those investments. He transferred them to his kids and grandkids.

Think about the audacity of that.

Americans lost more than $11 BILLION to crypto-related fraud last year. Those are people losing retirement savings, college funds, down payments, and in some cases their life savings.

The government is supposed to use its power to protect you from people trying to take your money. And yet, the guy making those decisions used that power to protect and help himself and left you more exposed to fraud.

For nearly two long and painful years, Americans have watched in helpless horror as our neighbors continue to be stolen from their homes and shot in the street by agents of the Trump Administration. Last night’s attempted murder of a New Yorker in front of his five-year-old son was far from the first disgraceful incident of its kind, but it must be the last. We demand that ICE leave our city immediately, and we are too disgusted to accept any delay.

While the Trump Administration’s government-sanctioned abuses have shocked our collective conscience and sickened our society, we cannot say that we are surprised to see them befall our communities. I fought bitterly to prevent Donald Trump and his congressional lackeys from empowering ICE with hundreds of billions in taxpayer dollars, because I was certain that these vile, unconstitutional crimes were an inevitability under this president’s watch. 

In fact, these depravities are the only promise Donald Trump has kept, serving as more red meat for his MAGA followers. Every incident is just another dreadful reminder of the resources that could have been spent positioning our society towards a brighter future. Not pulling the darkest chapters of our past back to the present.

ICE has proven itself nothing more than a vigilante weapon for the white nationalists to tear away at our multiracial democracy. It is a rogue agency, built by and for broken men. The only path forward is to rip that power away entirely, before ICE has any opportunity to further its relentless escalation of violence and despair in America. 

I therefore call upon Secretary Mullin to immediately remove ICE from sanctuary cities like New York City and all others his agents have invaded. The choice is his – however, the power is ours. Go out and vote!

text:
As the Co-Chair of the Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus, I welcome tonight's decision by Secretary of State Chris Bryant to ban the controversial Orange Order march in Drumcree. I am pleased that our calls for intervention have been heard, and I am grateful for the remarkable courage displayed by the residents of the Garvaghy Road during a time of considerable tension and unease. Tonight is their victory.

With this announcement, 28 years of precedent has been upheld. This march is an affront to the Garvaghy Road residents and those who have committed their lives to advancing peace and reconciliation on the island of Ireland. This has been a deeply divisive issue for years, and after three decades of hard-earned progress, allowing the march to proceed would have put that very progress in jeopardy.

As a guarantor of the Good Friday Agreement, the United States has a vested interest in seeing the principles of the accord upheld. This is a great day for the residents of Garvaghy Road and the next generation who seek nothing more than a shared future.
